subject: Human Evolution
title: Building with Bones
description: Learn Building with Bones in one minute.

hook.text: At Mezhyrich in Ukraine, a dwelling was built from 149 mammoth bones—skulls, tusks, and jawbones stacked.

buildup.text: On the treeless steppe, wood was scarce. Mammoth bones were the best structural material available.

discovery.text: These bone huts date to 15,000 years ago and could shelter small family groups through brutal winters.

twist.text: Some sites have multiple huts arranged in camps, suggesting organized communities, not lone families.

climax.text: Building permanent shelters from megafauna remains shows engineering and long-term planning on the steppe.

punchline.text: Mammoths became the bricks of ice age homes.

quiz.question: Why did ice age humans use mammoth bones for shelter?
options: Wood was scarce on the steppe, and bones were strong and available
